verdict.rationale: The office publishes forms for one delegated third-party role: appointing or changing a registered agent, plus a Commercial Registered Agent registration for agents representing more than 10 companies. It also references 'Authorized Users' for UCC e-filing. Nothing in the evidence spells out what such third parties may or may not do on an entity's behalf, or which signatures must stay personal. Missing for 10: a published scope-of-authority definition for agents, filers and authorized users; rules on which filings require a personal signature from an officer or member; general authorization or power-of-attorney forms for third-party filers; any independent or hands-on corroboration.
